topics.label: Introduction and course learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture series and outlines the specific learning objectives.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and tissue-level foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the molecular and developmental origins of cancer as a breakdown of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture while examining experimental models used to study them.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, and metastatic progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the histological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, detailing the processes of tissue invasion, stepwise progression, and metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and clinical mechanisms of disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the formal naming conventions for classifying tumors and describe the pathological mechanisms through which neoplastic growths cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence in humans and across multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the epidemiological occurrence of various tumor types in human populations and compare cancer incidence patterns across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and organ-specific cancer screening methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale and clinical symptoms prompting early cancer detection and evaluate the efficacy and challenges of screening programs across different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Closing housekeeping and review
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks and instructions for upcoming practicals and review sessions.
